prompt:
An intermediary arrives. The letter is short, precise, and carries the seal of a household that has not existed for two generations.

The First Architect writes: 'We have known of each other for some time. I do not pretend otherwise. You have surfaced my work and I have watched yours. Two people who have lived this long do not meet in the square. They send a letter first. Decide what shape ours will have.'

branches.label: Propose a division of labour — no acts in each other's strongholds.
branches.result: The First Architect replies within the season. 'A frame is easier to defend than an ambition. We can work within this.' A truce takes hold; the society's ops in your known strongholds will slow for two years.

branches.label: Offer a piece of intelligence they could not have by now.
branches.result: The Architect thanks you in prose that could be carved into stone. The channel is now warm — letters flow — but no truce is signed. They have taken the gift and remembered it.

branches.label: Refuse to commit. Insist every encounter be case-by-case.
branches.result: The reply is cool. 'Then we are strangers in the same century.' The channel stays open but the tone is winter. No truce; no warmth.

branches.label: Name a target: Macedon's succession. Propose joint work.
branches.result: A week's silence, then: 'We will move in the same direction from different doors.' An emergent succession mandate opens against Macedon, shaped by the Architects' preferences.
